f41ow4:313: TokenSpeed's support for Prefill/Decode separation (PD separation) reveals its insight into traffic patterns in Agent scenarios: during Agent execution, the Prefill phase (processing the input prompt) is compute-intensive but highly parallelizable, while the Decode phase (generating output tokens) is memory-bandwidth-intensive and requires stable latency. The two have fundamentally different resource demands; mixed deployment causes resource contention and tail latency jitter. PD separation allows requests to be dispatched to different resource pools based on request type, enabling finer-grained resource utilization control and more stable tail latency. This is especially critical for Agent scenarios requiring low-latency tool calls — after each tool call returns, the Agent needs to quickly ingest the result and continue executing, so tail latency fluctuations directly amplify into overall task execution time variance.

yrflc0:319: TokenSpeed uses compiler-level SPMD parallel modeling, delegating computation graph analysis and task assignment to the compiler. Compared with hand-tuned CUDA kernels, the compiler approach offers better scalability in multi-GPU scenarios — when GPU count increases, the compiler can automatically rebalance the compute load, whereas hand-optimized kernels need to be retuned for each specific topology. However, the challenge of the compiler approach is: for extreme optimization of specific model architectures (e.g., particular Attention variants), compiler-generated code may lag hand-optimized code by 10-20%. TokenSpeed's solution is a pluggable kernel mechanism that lets users insert hand-optimized kernels within the large-scale parallel framework, combining "the convenience of a compiler with the ultimate performance of hand tuning."
